convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to call external indicator 'BBands_Stop_v1' and includes TradeAlgorithms.mqh for trade execution logic, both of which require manual recreation in Python

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars required before calculation
UpSignalTime - timestamp for buy signal bar alignment
DnSignalTime - timestamp for sell signal bar alignment

other_exits: Long closes when DnValue[1] is nonzero (sell signal appears) and BuyPosClose is enabled
Short closes when UpValue[1] is nonzero (buy signal appears) and SellPosClose is enabled

position_sizing.conditional_logic: negative MM value = fixed lot size (0.1 lots); positive MM value = share of deposit fraction

custom_logic_notes: Signal uses BBands_Stop_v1 custom indicator with 4 buffers: buffer 4=UpBand values, buffer 1=DnBand values. Entry signal on bar [1] (previous confirmed bar), confirmed by non-zero value on bar [0] (current bar). The UpValue[1]!=0 check means the upper Bollinger stop line is active (price touched/penetrated the band), signaling a buy zone. DnValue[1]!=0 signals a sell zone. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose are boolean input gates that can independently enable/disable each direction's entry and exit. SignalBar input (default=1) controls which bar index is used for signal detection. When SignalBar=0, the EA evaluates on every tick without waiting for a new bar.
python_conversion_notes: Must recreate the BBands_Stop_v1 indicator logic: it computes Bollinger Bands with an offset factor (MoneyRisk), returning upper/lower stop levels in separate buffers. The nonzero-value convention for signal detection must be preserved. TradeAlgorithms.mqh must be reverse-engineered for BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose functions, including the MM conditional lot sizing (negative=fixed lots, positive=deposit fraction). The CIsNewBar class and LoadHistory function also come from TradeAlgorithms.mqh and need Python equivalents. SL/TP are in points and likely need digit-adjustment (multiply by 10) for 5-digit brokers since the values are large (1000/2000 points).
